title: Quantus POC benchmarking targets & measurement plan
summary: POC scoping focused on defining latency vs throughput targets, measurement methodology, and workload sizing. Agreed to run two benchmark waves: micro latency (single-request, cold/warm TTFT) and sustained throughput (TPOT-style, p95/p99 tail analysis) with a shared harness and production-sampled traffic. Security and deployment constraints (VPC, KMS) noted; Redwood to propose test config and schedule lab run.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2025-07-15 14:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Samira Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Brooks (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (Quantus Head of AI), Luis Ortega (Quantus Eng Manager), Priya Singh (Quantus Platform)

[00:00] Samira: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you squeezing this in. Quick agenda — we want to align on the POC success criteria for latency and throughput, agree the measurement plan, and lock a few dates. Is that good?
[00:12] Maya: Yep that sounds right. We really need clear pass/fail — engineering wants to know if we can hit p95 120ms for short prompts and also sustain X TPS for heavier workloads.
[00:22] Ethan: Got it. Maybe to start, quick definitions so we don't mix terms — we often talk about TTFT, first-token latency, and then sustained throughput (we sometimes call TPOT in internal notes) which is more about tokens-per-second under load. For the POC I recommend two waves: micro latency tests (cold vs warm, prefix caching effect) and sustained runs that emulate realistic concurrency.
[00:41] Luis: Quick question: our product has two primary flows — short chat prompts (avg 12 tokens out) and document summarize (avg 450 tokens out). We'll need both profiles exercised.
[00:53] Ethan: Perfect, so we'll define two workload classes: chat-short and doc-long. For chat-short we'll target p95 and p99 numbers on first token and end-to-end response. For doc-long, we measure steady-state throughput and per-token latency distribution.
[01:06] Priya: Also important — our security folks insist on VPC peering and customer-managed KMS for the POC. Any special requirements from Redwood?
[01:14] Samira: We can run the lab with a private peered VPC, the control plane will still be managed but the data path sits in your VPC. KMS integration is supported; we'll need an IAM role and a KMS key ARN from you. We'll capture this in the runbook.
[01:26] Maya: Great. On targets — to give you a sense: for chat-short we *hope* for p95 <= 120ms and p99 <= 260ms (TTFT-first token); for doc-long we want to understand tokens/sec at 95th percentile tail under 200 concurrent users. But we're flexible if you recommend different SLOs.
[01:44] Ethan: Those are reasonable starting points; two notes: 1) TTFT measured cold (no KV cache) will be higher, so we should define cold vs warm windows, and 2) measuring p95 for end-to-end vs first-token are different signals — we'll report both.
[01:58] Speaker 1 (muffled): yeah.. and quantization will affect shapes —
[02:03] Ethan: Right, if we use 4-bit quantized model variants it changes latency characteristics; we'll document the variant used. For the POC I suggest we run baseline on the exact model you plan to serve in prod plus one smaller quantized variant to show cost/latency tradeoffs.
[02:19] Luis: For throughput: do you recommend burst-style ramp then steady state? Our traffic has diurnal spikes but for POC engineering wants the steady-state numbers.
[02:28] Ethan: Standard best practice — 3-phase runs: ramp-up (10 minutes), steady-state (30 minutes), cool-down (5 minutes). We'll do multiple runs and compute p50/p95/p99 on the steady-state period. We'll also capture CPU/GPU utilization, queue depths, and dropped requests.
[02:44] Maya: How do we handle warmup for KV cache / prefix caching? We don't have a warm cache in a fresh deployment.
[02:50] Samira: Two approaches: 1) simulate cold start by clearing caches and doing single-shot requests, and 2) run synthetic warmup traffic matching the top-20 prefixes so steady-state represents a warmed service. We'll provide tooling to pre-populate KV cache. We'll record both cold and warm results so you can see delta.
[03:06] Priya: Measurement fidelity is important for our procurement team — can you produce reproducible runs and the raw logs?
[03:12] Samira: Yes, we'll share the harness outputs, raw traces, Prometheus metrics export, and the run artifacts. We'll also attach the JMX / per-token timings and the script used to compute p95/p99.
[03:22] Maya: On datasets — do you want us to send prod sample prompts or is synthetic acceptable?
[03:27] Ethan: Ideally prod-sampled prompts (anonymized) so latency shape and token lengths match your real traffic. If that's not possible, a carefully crafted synthetic distribution that matches token length histogram is okay.
[03:36] Luis: We'll prepare a 100k sample with rate-limited sensitive fields removed.
[03:40] Samira: Excellent. We'll need a mapping of prompt types to probability weights for the harness. For success criteria, let's codify a pass/fail for each workload class: e.g., chat-short pass if p95(first-token) <= 120ms AND p99(first-token) <= 260ms for warm runs; doc-long pass if sustained tokens/sec >= your target with p95 per-token latency below X ms. We can be more explicit once you provide exact throughput target.
[04:03] Maya: For doc-long we'd start with target of 8 tokens/sec per user at 200 concurrent — effectively 1600 tokens/sec end-to-end but let's see what Redwood measures.
[04:12] Ethan: We'll translate that into concurrency and QPS in the harness. Also we'll instrument to report tail latency per 100-token buckets so we can see degradation as sequence length increases.
[04:23] Speaker 2 (background): -uh-huh-
[04:26] Samira: On reporting — we'll deliver a benchmark report with charts: latency CDFs (first-token and end-to-end), throughput over time, resource utilization, error rate, and a recommended configuration (batching, quantization level, autoscale policy). We'll also include an appendix with raw CSVs.
[04:40] Maya: Good. Any thoughts on statistical significance? We need confidence that differences are real, not noise.
[04:46] Ethan: We'll run at least 3 independent steady-state runs and compute mean and 95% confidence intervals for p95/p99. For borderline cases we can extend runs to reduce variance.
[04:55] Maya: About network — our infra sits in GCP us-west1, do you have region parity?
[05:02] Samira: We have hosted capacity in us-west and can run lab in that region; for Dedicated/Private we can pin to your region. We'll note cross-region latency in the run artifacts if any.
[05:11] Priya: Security checklist — SOC2 attestation, SAML SSO for console, RBAC for run artifacts, audit logs — do you provide SOC2 and can we see audit log examples?
[05:20] Samira: Yes, Redwood SOC2 Type II is available. We'll send the security pack and a sanitized audit log sample. SAML and RBAC configs are part of the onboarding.
[05:29] Luis: For the lab run networking we'll need an IP allowlist and egress restrictions — we'll validate that during setup.
[05:35] Samira: We'll provide the IP ranges and a small setup guide.
[05:38] Maya: One more question — how do you measure 'first token' for streaming vs non-streaming models? We stream in prod.
[05:44] Ethan: Good point — when streaming, first-token is time to first byte streamed; for non-streaming it's model decode time for first token. We'll align on a consistent metric and mark which runs were streaming-enabled.
[05:55] Speaker 1: i think also consider the effect of batching at higher concurrency —
[05:58] Ethan: Right — batching reduces per-token latency but can increase tail for single requests. We'll capture batch sizes and distribution; our harness will log batch composition per request.
[06:08] Maya: Great. On timeline, can we get an end-to-end POC in three weeks?
[06:13] Samira: Timeline suggestion: share harness and measurement template by 7/17; Quantus provide samples and env access by 7/22; lab run week of 7/28; results review ~8/1. That fits a 3-week-ish cadence.
[06:26] Priya: That works for us, subject to security review gating the VPC peering.
[06:30] Ethan: One operational note — for Dedicated deployments we'll show autoscale policies and burst buckets; for the POC we can simulate limited capacity to show graceful fallback.
[06:40] Maya: Okay. Any immediate blockers?
[06:43] Luis: We'll need an NDA addendum for benchmark runs, but procurement can handle that fast. Also we need to flag potential budget limits for private deployments.
[06:53] Samira: Noted. We'll coordinate legal and procurement contacts after this call.
[06:58] [Recap]
[06:59] Samira: Quick recap — two benchmark waves (micro latency and sustained throughput), produce cold and warm results, target metrics for chat-short and doc-long to be confirmed, Redwood to provide harness and runbook, Quantus to provide prompt samples and VPC/KMS details. Next call to review run results.
[07:20] Maya: Thanks, that helps. We'll aim to get artifacts over this week.
[07:25] Samira: Perfect — we'll follow up with the repo link, measurement template, and a calendar invite for the lab run. Thanks all.

End of transcript (notes: occasional background noise; some speaker attribution guessed by auto-transcribe).
